basic_identification.full_title: Agro Textiles — Windshield Nets for Agriculture and Horticulture Purposes — Specification

scope.summary: This standard prescribes constructional and other performance requirements for windshield nets manufactured from mono filament yarns for agriculture and horticulture purposes to protect the flora from damage caused by high-speed wind by reducing or blocking the amount of wind passing through them.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Agrotech Textiles / Crop Protection Materials)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all Windshield Nets manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 17356:2020 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified agricultural windshield nets in India is a statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic monofilament windshield nets.

requirements.detail: Every roll or bundle of certified windshield net must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 17356) printed on a secure label or edge tape.

Windshield nets must be manufactured from high-quality HDPE monofilament yarns conforming to Clauses 4.1 and 4.1.1 of IS 17356:2020. The monofilament yarn shall be thoroughly UV-stabilised (for a minimum of 3 years resistance) and contain non-toxic pigments.
The fabric used in the manufacture of windshield nets shall be knitted on warp knitting machines and shall have a width as per the agreement between the buyer and the seller.
The standard classifies windshield nets into two primary types: Type 1 and Type 2. Separate samples of each type must be tested for scope certification.

Windshield nets must be provided with eyelets (or brass sail type eyelets conforming to IS 4084) along the length and width of the fabric as shown in Fig. 1 to facilitate secure installation. Typical edge-to-edge distances, eyelet-to-eyelet distances, and eyelet lengths must be declared.
Applicable for coloured windshield nets only. The colour fastness to artificial light must achieve a rating of 4 or better when evaluated using Xenon arc fading lamp test methods as per ISO 105-B02.

Windshield nets must resist severe localized forces. The bursting pressure of the fabric must be at least 10 kgf/cm² for Type 1 and 14 kgf/cm² for Type 2, evaluated as per hydraulic or pneumatic methods of IS 1966.

The primary aerodynamic purpose of the net is wind reduction. The wind blockage must be at least 18 percent for Type 1 and 35 percent for Type 2, tested as per the blower and measurement chamber method outlined in Annex C.

requirements.requirement_type: Retention of Breaking Strength after UV weathering
requirements.detail: To guarantee durability under intense sun, the fabric must undergo accelerated UV weathering. The retained breaking strength (warpway and weftway) must be at least 85 percent of the original actual fabric strength, tested per Annex B and IS 1969 (Part 1).

Finished netting rolls must be clean, flat, uniform, and free from manufacturing defects such as missing yarns, distorted meshes, or scale. Colour or pigment mixture shall conform to sealed client reference samples.

For quality audit inspections, random samples must be selected per Table 2 (Scale of Sampling). Lots are defined as monofilament windshield net rolls/bundles of the same construction and type dispatched under one dispatch note.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 17356 : 2020 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing UV-stabilized high-density polyethylene (HDPE) monofilament windshield nets used in the agriculture and horticulture sectors. These nets act as mesh barriers placed around open fields, orchards, and nurseries to protect crops from mechanical damage, dust, insects, and frost caused by high-speed winds. Under India's statutory Agro Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all windshield nets supplied to the Indian market must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). The standard classifies nets into Type 1 and Type 2, enforcing strict mechanical and physical limits—including a minimum wind blockage performance of 18% to 35%, a minimum bursting pressure of 10 to 14 kgf/cm², and a minimum breaking strength retention of 85% after accelerated UV weathering to guarantee long-term outdoor service life.
